artifacts.summary: Implementation summary: source-side tier-3 cross-repo consumer freshness report, all 7 plan phases completed

completion_data.completion_summary: Added a git-tracked known-consumer registry, a new check-consumer-freshness.sh fleet report (with --discover reconciliation), a guarded post-deploy stale-consumer hook in deploy-headless.sh, and a non-blocking consecutive-ignore escalation on the existing tier-1 WARN. Verified live against all 8 real consumer repos and two real deploy-headless.sh runs in this repo; the 0/1/2/3 exit-code contract is unchanged.

memory_candidates.content: When a script under agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/ writes an ephemeral runtime file rooted at <repo_root>/specs/ (not under .claude/), the gitignore coverage MUST go in the repo's own top-level .gitignore (or the documented 'Consumer Repo Setup' block in orchestrator-runtime-files.md for other consumer repos) -- NOT in agent-system/extensions/core/root-files/.gitignore. root-files/.gitignore only deploys into a consumer's .claude/ directory, so a specs/-rooted pattern placed there silently resolves to .claude/specs/... and matches nothing. Verify by grepping every existing sibling ephemeral-file pattern (e.g. .orchestrator-churn-state.json) across agent-system/extensions/core/ before trusting a plan's stated gitignore target.

manifest.json's provides.context can declare a whole DIRECTORY (e.g. 'reference'), meaning any new file dropped into that source-store directory (e.g. context/reference/known-consumer-repos.json) deploys automatically into every consumer's .claude/ tree without a separate manifest entry -- useful when a new reference file should ship everywhere, but a trap if the intent was 'source-repo-only metadata'. Confirm the intended deploy scope of a new context/ file against manifest.json's provides.context BEFORE writing it, not after.

When testing --discover-style filesystem-scan reconciliation logic that matches on a real repo's directory layout (e.g. source_dir starting with '<repo>/agent-system/extensions/'), the test fixture MUST mirror that same layout, not a flattened stand-in -- a fixture that puts extension dirs directly under the fake source repo root (rather than under agent-system/extensions/) will make every path-prefix filter silently fail to match, producing a false negative that looks like a script bug rather than a fixture bug.
